# Caries Prevalence

```{r}

###############
# =========================================================
# Dental caries distribution across salivary immune phenotypes
# HUU + HEU + HI
# =========================================================

library(tidyverse)

# =========================================================
# 1. Combine metadata from all groups
# =========================================================

caries_all <- bind_rows(
  
  meta_sub_HUU %>%
    mutate(Group = "HUU"),
  
  meta_sub_HEU %>%
    mutate(Group = "HEU"),
  
  meta_sub_HI %>%
    mutate(Group = "HI")
  
)


# Check structure
table(caries_all$Group)
table(caries_all$Group, caries_all$Mclust_cluster)
table(caries_all$Group, caries_all$caries_IL)

caries_all$Group <- factor(caries_all$Group, levels = c("HUU", "HEU", "HI"))


# =========================================================
# 2. Phenotype-specific caries prevalence table
# =========================================================
#
# Prevalence:
# caries-positive children within each phenotype /
# total children in that phenotype
#
# Also calculate:
# proportion of all caries cases contributed by phenotype
# =========================================================

caries_summary <- caries_all %>%
  
  group_by(
    Group,
    Mclust_cluster
  ) %>%
  
  summarise(
    
    n_phenotype = n(),
    
    caries_cases = sum(
      caries_IL == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    no_caries = sum(
      caries_IL == 0,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    prevalence_percent =
      100 * caries_cases / n_phenotype,
    
    .groups = "drop"
    
  ) %>%
  
  group_by(Group) %>%
  
  mutate(
    
    total_caries_group =
      sum(caries_cases),
    
    proportion_of_group_caries_percent =
      100 * caries_cases /
      total_caries_group
    
  ) %>%
  
  ungroup() %>%
  
  mutate(
    
    prevalence_percent =
      round(prevalence_percent, 1),
    
    proportion_of_group_caries_percent =
      round(
        proportion_of_group_caries_percent,
        1
      )
    
  )


# View final table
caries_summary

caries_summary <- data.frame(caries_summary)
caries_summary

# =========================================================
# 3. Save/export table
# =========================================================

#write.csv(
 # caries_summary,
  #"caries_distribution_by_saliva_phenotype.csv",
  #row.names = FALSE
#)



# =========================================================
# Plot: phenotype-specific caries prevalence
# Groups together on X-axis
# =========================================================

caries_prev_plot <- ggplot(
  caries_summary,
  aes(
    x = Group,
    y = prevalence_percent,
    fill = factor(Mclust_cluster)
  )
) +
  
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        caries_cases,
        "/",
        n_phenotype,
        "\n(",
        prevalence_percent,
        "%)"
      )
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "1" = "#D73027",
      "2" = "#2C7BB6",
      "3" = "#1B9E77"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "1" = "S1",
      "2" = "S2",
      "3" = "S3"
    ),
    name = "Salivary immune phenotype"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      max(
        caries_summary$prevalence_percent,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) * 1.25
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 14
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Dental caries prevalence across salivary immune phenotypes",
    x = "HIV exposure/infection group",
    y = "Caries prevalence (%)"
  ) +
  
  theme(
    
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),
    
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      color = "black"
    ),
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0.5,
      face = "bold",
      size = 16
    ),
    
    legend.position = "top"
  )


caries_prev_plot



# =========================================================
# 5. Optional: plot distribution of all caries cases
# =========================================================
#
# Answers:
# "Where are the caries-positive children located?"
#
# Different question from prevalence
# =========================================================

# =========================================================
# Plot: distribution of caries cases across phenotypes
# Groups together on X-axis
# =========================================================

caries_case_distribution_plot <- ggplot(
  caries_summary,
  aes(
    x = Group,
    y = proportion_of_group_caries_percent,
    fill = factor(Mclust_cluster)
  )
) +
  
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        caries_cases,
        " cases"
      )
    ),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.35,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "1" = "#D73027",
      "2" = "#2C7BB6",
      "3" = "#1B9E77"
    ),
    labels = c(
      "1" = "S1",
      "2" = "S2",
      "3" = "S3"
    ),
    name = "Salivary immune phenotype"
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      0,
      max(
        caries_summary$proportion_of_group_caries_percent,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ) * 1.25
    ),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 14
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title =
      "Distribution of caries cases across salivary immune phenotypes",
    
    x =
      "HIV exposure/infection group",
    
    y =
      "Proportion of group caries cases (%)"
  ) +
  
  theme(
    
    axis.text.x =
      element_text(
        color = "black"
      ),
    
    axis.text.y =
      element_text(
        color = "black"
      ),
    
    plot.title =
      element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = 16
      ),
    
    legend.position = "top"
  )


caries_case_distribution_plot


###### Prevalence of caries across groups 

fit_group <- glm(
  caries_IL ~ study_group + host_age + host_sex,
  data = caries_all,
  family = binomial
)

summary(fit_group)

exp(cbind(
  OR = coef(fit_group),
  confint(fit_group)
))

table(caries_all$study_group)


```
